title: Searching for news used to mean digging through a pile of links.
body:
For years, we have been trained to ask a search engine a question and then sort through ten blue links to find the answer. We did the heavy lifting. We read the headlines, scanned the snippets, and clicked around until we found what we needed. It was effective, but it was slow.

AI search is changing that dynamic entirely. Now, instead of hunting for a source that might have the answer, we are starting to get the answer directly. This shifts the role of the reader from being a researcher to being a consumer of synthesized information.

But there is a catch. When the machine gives you the answer, you lose the context of where that answer came from. You miss the nuance of the original reporting. Efficiency is great, but understanding the source of your information matters just as much.

At Headlinne, we are trying to find the middle ground. We believe you should get the speed of AI without losing the connection to the journalism that actually did the work. It is about getting smarter answers without losing the bigger picture.
cta: If you want to see how we are approaching this, take a look at HEADLINNE.com.
